segmentation.text: Whenever a motor vehicle is being operated
on the traveled portion of the highway, or shoulder adjacent thereto,
during the times specified in
the driver shall use a distribution of light, or composite beam,
directed high enough and of sufficient intensity to reveal persons and vehicles at a safe distance in advance of the vehicle,
subject to the following requirements and limitations:
Whenever a driver of a vehicle approaches an oncoming vehicle within 500 feet,
the driver shall use a distribution of light, or composite beam, so aimed that the glaring rays are not projected into the eyes of the oncoming driver.
The lowermost distribution of light, or composite beam, specified in subsection 2 of
shall be deemed to avoid glare at all times, regardless of road contour and loading.

elements.justification: 'motor vehicle' is a term the definitions table admits as the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails'); it is claimed as the aggregate, never expanded into classes. 'is being operated' names no class: it is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency).

Same words as the index mapping of NRS_484D_165_3 ('upon the traveled portion of a highway or shoulder adjacent thereto'). st.roadway: 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder' is the traveled portion; st.shoulder: 'the part of the highway beside the roadway not intended for vehicular traffic'; st.on_way ties the roadway or shoulder to 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on'; st.highway is the defined highway (DEF-NRS-484A-095: 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority'), contract 'the entire public way between its boundary lines'; its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: the roadway' does not apply because the roadway is carried by its own atom. rel.occupies anchors the subject: 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (roadway, shoulder ...)'.

The times are borrowed from NRS-484D-100-1: '(a) At any time from one-half hour after sunset to one-half hour before sunrise; (b) At any other time when, because of insufficient light or unfavorable atmospheric conditions, persons and vehicles on the highway are not clearly discernible at a distance of 1,000 feet ahead; and (c) When directed by an official traffic control device.' (a) is env.darkness, 'insufficient natural light; the boundary relative to sunset and sunrise is a reading parameter'. (b) is env.darkness for 'insufficient light' and env.visibility, 'visibility distance (fog, dust, smoke)', below the borrowed 1,000 feet for 'unfavorable atmospheric conditions'. (c) needs a device directing the display of lamps that governs the subject's travel region; dev.regulatory_sign ('a point regulation by catalogue code') read through dev.governs and the subject's occupied travel region (rel.occupies, st.travel_region) is the nearest carrier, but its closed code list holds no code directing lamps: the gap on this span states it. Same words as the index mapping of NRS_484D_100_1 for (a), (b) and (c).

sig.headlamp: 'headlamp state in {off, low_beam, high_beam}'. 'use a distribution of light, or composite beam' is a lit headlamp beam, low_beam or high_beam, and not off. The atom has no not-a-stand-in clause. 'the driver' is read through the vehicle's own lamp state (observable_reading, agency).

In this node the words are the limitation to which the first duty is 'subject': while an oncoming vehicle is within 500 feet the beam need not reach the safe distance, only be lit. 'a vehicle' and 'an oncoming vehicle' are the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle. rel.oncoming: 'headings opposed and closing: the cosine of the angle between the headings is below the negative of its tolerance' is 'approaches an oncoming vehicle'; its exclusion (the direction a road user approaches an intersection from) does not apply, no intersection approach is read. rel.surface_gap: 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies' carries 'within 500 feet' between the two vehicles; it is preferred to rel.centre_distance, whose contract warns that it 'overstates a clearance by about the two half-extents'.

operationalizations.standard: directed high enough and of sufficient intensity to reveal persons and vehicles at a safe distance in advance of the vehicle
operationalizations.convention: stopping-sight-distance model (AASHTO Green Book): a beam reveals persons and vehicles at a safe distance where the distance it lights ahead is at least the subject's stopping distance, speed times the perception-reaction time plus speed squared over twice the braking deceleration. The upper beam is the uppermost distribution the equipment law provides and is read as meeting the bound; the lower beam meets it where p.low_beam_sight_reach is at least that stopping distance at the subject's speed (kin.speed).

compositions.quote: (a) At any time from one-half hour after sunset to one-half hour before sunrise; (b) At any other time when, because of insufficient light or unfavorable atmospheric conditions, persons and vehicles on the highway are not clearly discernible at a distance of 1,000 feet ahead; and (c) When directed by an official traffic control device.
compositions.why: The words borrow only 'the times specified' in NRS 484D.100(1): its three time qualifiers (a), (b) and (c), each kept whole (the half-hour sunset and sunrise boundary, the 1,000-foot discernibility, the device's direction). They do not borrow that law's duty to display lamps, its class of vehicles, its highway condition or its exception for parked vehicles: this duty applies at those times whether or not NRS 484D.100's rule is engaged for the subject or complied with, so no rule of it need apply, hold or be complied with.

applicability: The subject is a motor vehicle (DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle) whose footprint occupies a roadway or a shoulder that lies on a highway, at an observation at which one of the borrowed times holds: env.darkness; or env.visibility below 1,000 feet; or a device directing the display of lamps governs a travel region the subject occupies (this last alternative has no atom: gap).
obligation: At every such observation the subject's headlamp (sig.headlamp) is low_beam or high_beam, not off. Where it is low_beam, the low beam reaches far enough: p.low_beam_sight_reach is at least kin.speed * p.driver_reaction_time + kin.speed^2 / (2 * p.following_decel_dry) of the subject, unless (s8) some other road user of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle is oncoming to the subject (rel.oncoming with tolerance p.oncoming_heading_cos) with a surface gap (rel.surface_gap) of at most 500 feet. high_beam always meets the reach requirement.

narrowings.why: 'is being operated' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion on the way; whoever or whatever controls it.
'the driver shall use' is read as the subject vehicle's own headlamp state.

The safe distance is read on a dry-surface stopping model; a wet or icy surface, which would lengthen the distance, is not read. The beam's height and intensity are read only through which beam is lit, the upper beam meeting the bound whatever the speed. The limitation for following another vehicle closely, which this line does not state, is not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A passenger car (motor vehicle) drives on the roadway of a highway with env.darkness true; its sig.headlamp is off; no other vehicle is present.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same darkness and roadway; the car's sig.headlamp is high_beam at 25 m/s; no other vehicle is present.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: Daytime: env.darkness false, env.visibility several kilometres, no regulatory sign governs the car's lane; headlamp off.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Darkness, car on the roadway, sig.headlamp not observed on the source.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Darkness, car on the roadway at 25 m/s with sig.headlamp low_beam, no other vehicle present: the stopping distance exceeds the low-beam reach.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: Darkness, car at 25 m/s on low_beam while an oncoming car closes with a surface gap of 100 m (within 500 feet).

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: Darkness, car at 8 m/s on low_beam, alone: the stopping distance lies within the low-beam reach.

param_proposals.name: p.low_beam_sight_reach
param_proposals.convention: the distance ahead a passenger-car low beam lights the road in darkness enough to see an obstacle
param_proposals.source: low-beam seeing-distance studies of passenger-car headlamps

param_proposals.name: p.driver_reaction_time
param_proposals.convention: perception-reaction time of an alert driver to an expected hazard in the stopping-distance model

param_proposals.name: p.following_decel_dry
param_proposals.convention: braking deceleration of a passenger vehicle on a dry paved surface (coefficient of friction about 0.6)
param_proposals.source: braking friction tables of accident reconstruction

param_proposals.name: p.oncoming_heading_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest angle off exactly opposed headings (about 25 degrees) at which two vehicles count as proceeding in opposite directions
param_proposals.source: heading noise of tracked vehicles on gently curving roads

gaps.proposal: | `dev.lamps_on_sign` | an official sign or device directing road users to display lighted lamps (headlamps on) where it governs, the stretch it governs read through `dev.governs` | general |
gaps.nearest: dev.regulatory_sign: 'a point regulation by catalogue code' whose closed code list (no_left_turn ... no_trucks) holds no code directing the display of lamps; dev.zone_sign: its kinds (school ... trail) name no lamps-on zone. Whether lamps are required on the stretch the subject drives (the time of the duty) is the distinction no atom decides; the same gap is pending as smoke31-1111-0039:G21 on NRS-484D-100-1.

segmentation.text: Whenever a motor vehicle is being operated
on the traveled portion of the highway, or shoulder adjacent thereto,
during the times specified in
the driver shall use a distribution of light, or composite beam,
directed high enough and of sufficient intensity to reveal persons and vehicles at a safe distance in advance of the vehicle,
subject to the following requirements and limitations:
Whenever a driver of a vehicle approaches an oncoming vehicle within 500 feet,
the driver shall use a distribution of light, or composite beam, so aimed that the glaring rays are not projected into the eyes of the oncoming driver.
The lowermost distribution of light, or composite beam, specified in subsection 2 of
shall be deemed to avoid glare at all times, regardless of road contour and loading.

elements.justification: 'motor vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails'), claimed as the aggregate. 'is being operated' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency).

Same words as the index mapping of NRS_484D_165_3. st.roadway: 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder' is the traveled portion; st.shoulder: 'the part of the highway beside the roadway'; st.on_way ties either to 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on'; st.highway is the defined highway (DEF-NRS-484A-095: 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority'); its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: the roadway' does not apply, the roadway having its own atom. rel.occupies anchors the subject's footprint on the roadway or shoulder.

Borrowed from NRS-484D-100-1: '(a) At any time from one-half hour after sunset to one-half hour before sunrise; (b) At any other time when, because of insufficient light or unfavorable atmospheric conditions, persons and vehicles on the highway are not clearly discernible at a distance of 1,000 feet ahead; and (c) When directed by an official traffic control device.' (a) env.darkness, 'insufficient natural light; the boundary relative to sunset and sunrise is a reading parameter'; (b) env.darkness or env.visibility ('visibility distance (fog, dust, smoke)') below the borrowed 1,000 feet; (c) a device directing lamps governing the subject's occupied travel region, nearest dev.regulatory_sign through dev.governs, rel.occupies and st.travel_region, whose code list holds no such code: the gap on this span. Same words as NRS_484D_100_1's mapping.

'a vehicle' and 'an oncoming vehicle' are the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle. rel.oncoming: 'headings opposed and closing' is 'approaches an oncoming vehicle'; its exclusion (direction of approach to an intersection) is not read here. rel.surface_gap: 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies' carries 'within 500 feet' between the two vehicles, rather than rel.centre_distance, which 'overstates a clearance by about the two half-extents'. 'a driver of' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency).

sig.headlamp: 'headlamp state in {off, low_beam, high_beam}'. A beam 'so aimed that the glaring rays are not projected into the eyes of the oncoming driver' is any state but high_beam: the lowermost beam is deemed to avoid glare (s10-s12), and the upper beam is the one whose rays are projected into an oncoming driver's eyes. No not-a-stand-in clause applies.

The lowermost beam borrowed from DEF-NRS-484D-210-1-2: 'There shall be a lowermost distribution of light, or composite beam, so aimed and of sufficient intensity to reveal persons and vehicles at a distance of at least 100 feet ahead' is the low_beam value of sig.headlamp ('headlamp state in {off, low_beam, high_beam}').

'deemed to avoid glare at all times' makes sig.headlamp low_beam compliant with s9 whatever the scene; 'regardless of road contour and loading' says no curvature, grade or load condition is read beside it.

compositions.quote: (a) At any time from one-half hour after sunset to one-half hour before sunrise; (b) At any other time when, because of insufficient light or unfavorable atmospheric conditions, persons and vehicles on the highway are not clearly discernible at a distance of 1,000 feet ahead; and (c) When directed by an official traffic control device.
compositions.why: The words borrow only 'the times specified' in NRS 484D.100(1): its three time qualifiers (a), (b) and (c), each kept whole (the half-hour sunset and sunrise boundary, the 1,000-foot discernibility, the device's direction). They do not borrow that law's duty to display lamps, its class of vehicles, its highway condition or its exception for parked vehicles: this duty applies at those times whether or not NRS 484D.100's rule is engaged for the subject or complied with, so no rule of it need apply, hold or be complied with.

compositions.quote: There shall be a lowermost distribution of light, or composite beam, so aimed and of sufficient intensity to reveal persons and vehicles at a distance of at least 100 feet ahead
compositions.why: The words borrow only what 'the lowermost distribution of light, or composite beam' is: the lower of the beams a motor vehicle's headlamps select between, the low beam. Whether the vehicle's equipment meets the aiming and intensity specification is not borrowed and need not hold; the deeming applies to the beam selected.

applicability: The subject is a motor vehicle (DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle) whose footprint occupies a roadway or a shoulder lying on a highway; one of the borrowed times holds (env.darkness; env.visibility below 1,000 feet; a lamps-on device governing the subject's travel region, which has no atom: gap); and some other road user of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle is oncoming to the subject (rel.oncoming, tolerance p.oncoming_heading_cos) with a surface gap (rel.surface_gap) of at most 500 feet.
obligation: At every such observation the subject's sig.headlamp is not high_beam (low_beam is deemed to avoid glare at all times; whether a beam is lit at all is the sibling duty's).

narrowings.why: 'is being operated' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion on the way.

'so aimed that the glaring rays are not projected into the eyes of the oncoming driver' is read through the beam selected: high_beam projects glare, low_beam is deemed not to; the actual aim of a lamp and the eye position of the oncoming driver are not read. An unlit headlamp projects no rays and is left to the sibling duty.
'the driver shall use' is read as the subject vehicle's own headlamp state.

segmentation.text: An authorized emergency vehicle
may be equipped with a siren, whistle or bell, capable of emitting sound audible under normal conditions from a distance of not less than 500 feet,
but the siren must not be used
except when the vehicle is operated in response to an emergency call
or in the immediate pursuit of an actual or suspected violator of the law,
in which event the driver of the vehicle may sound the siren to warn pedestrians and other drivers of his or her approach.
A driver of an emergency vehicle may operate the vehicle’s warning lamps without sounding the siren.

elements.justification: 'authorized emergency vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle ('a vehicle permitted to depart from certain traffic laws when equipped and operated in the manner provided by law'), claimed as the aggregate and never replaced by ru.emergency_vehicle.

sig.siren: 'a siren, whistle or bell sounding (audible; a source without audio declares it absent, and does not read a warning lamp as the sound)'. 'the siren must not be used' is the subject's own sig.siren not sounding. The exclusion of the warning lamp is respected: the lamp enters only the exception.

Responding to an emergency call is a purpose; ru.emergency_vehicle's contract says 'the class alone is not responding; its responding is conduct'. The conduct of a vehicle operated in response to a call is the display of its warning lamps: sig.warning_lamp, 'a warning lamp lit; colour in {red, blue, amber, white}, mode in {flashing, rotating, steady}', read with mode flashing or rotating. Its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: an audible warning' is respected: the lamp is never read as the siren.

Immediate pursuit of a violator is a purpose read through the same conduct: the pursuing vehicle displays its warning lamps, sig.warning_lamp 'a warning lamp lit', mode flashing or rotating; not read as an audible warning.

residues.why: A permission about equipment and its audible range; it imposes no duty on conduct and the rule judges only whether the siren sounds.

Restates the permission the exception (s4, s5) grants: in that event the siren may sound. The purpose 'to warn pedestrians and other drivers of his or her approach' is what a sounding siren does; the duty is the same whether or not these words are read.
A permission to show warning lamps without the siren; it imposes no duty, and the siren duty never judges lamps alone.

applicability: The subject is an authorized emergency vehicle (DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle), except at an observation at which it displays a warning lamp (sig.warning_lamp) in mode flashing or rotating, which is read as the vehicle operated in response to an emergency call or in immediate pursuit (s4, s5).
obligation: At every such observation the subject's sig.siren is not sounding.

narrowings.why: Operation in response to an emergency call is read through its conduct, the vehicle's warning lamps flashing or rotating; a response made without lamps is not recognised.
Immediate pursuit of an actual or suspected violator is read through the pursuing vehicle's warning lamps flashing or rotating; a pursuit without lamps is not recognised.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A police car (authorized emergency vehicle) drives with sig.siren sounding and no sig.warning_lamp lit.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The police car drives with sig.siren silent and no warning lamp lit.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject is a private passenger car, not an authorized emergency vehicle; its siren is not observed to sound.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The police car drives with no warning lamp lit; the source has no audio, sig.siren absent.

scenarios.name: branch_1

segmentation.text: Every motorcycle or moped
when being driven on the highway
is entitled to full use of the traffic lane it is occupying,
and a person shall not drive another motor vehicle
in a manner which would deprive any such motorcycle or moped of such use.

elements.justification: 'motorcycle' and 'moped' are the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-486-041::motorcycle ('every motor vehicle equipped with a seat or a saddle for the use of the driver and designed to travel on not more than three wheels') and DEF-NRS-486-038::moped; each is claimed as the aggregate, not as the class atoms ru.motorcycle and ru.moped. The motorcycle or moped is a road user quantified in the obligation, not a binder.

st.highway: 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders' is the defined highway (DEF-NRS-486-031: 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way maintained by a public authority'); its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: the roadway' does not apply, the whole way being meant. rel.occupies anchors the motorcycle's footprint on it. 'being driven' is read through the motorcycle's presence and controlled motion on the way (agency): a motorcycle halted in a lane in traffic is still being driven.

st.lane: 'a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles' is 'the traffic lane'; its exclusions (a half of the roadway, a lateral position within a lane) do not apply, the lane being the strip itself. 'it is occupying' is rel.occupies of the motorcycle and that lane: 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'. 'traffic lane' is a lane; no road users of the traffic aggregate are read by the word.

'another motor vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails'): the subject, a road user other than the motorcycle or moped. 'a person shall not drive' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency).

Depriving the motorcycle of full use of its lane is read as the subject sharing that lane beside it: the subject's footprint overlaps the same st.lane the motorcycle occupies (rel.occupies) while the two bodies are side by side, rel.longitudinal_overlap 'the bodies overlap along the subject's heading (side by side): the length the two footprints' projections on that axis share' at or above zero. The overlap is 'a projection, so neither a contact nor a distance between the bodies', and it is read only as side-by-side position, not contact.

applicability: The subject is a motor vehicle (DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle).
obligation: At every observation, for every road user m other than the subject (not same) that is of DEF-NRS-486-041::motorcycle or DEF-NRS-486-038::moped and occupies a highway, and every lane L that m occupies: it is not the case that the subject occupies L and rel.longitudinal_overlap of the subject and m is at or above zero.

narrowings.why: Depriving of full use is read as the subject's footprint sharing the motorcycle's lane while side by side with it; a closeness from behind or from the next lane that leaves the motorcycle's lane free of the subject's footprint is not read.
'a person shall not drive' is read through the subject vehicle's controlled motion.
'being driven' is read through the motorcycle's presence and controlled motion on the highway, whoever is at its controls.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car occupies lane L of a highway beside a motorcycle also occupying L; rel.longitudinal_overlap of car and motorcycle 2 m.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The car occupies lane L 20 m behind the motorcycle in L; rel.longitudinal_overlap negative.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject is a bicycle beside the motorcycle in L; a bicycle is not a motor vehicle.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The car and the motorcycle both occupy L; rel.longitudinal_overlap is not observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The car drives on the highway; no motorcycle or moped is in the scene.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The car occupies the adjacent lane only, side by side with the motorcycle in L.

segmentation.text: A person,
except a police officer in the performance of his or her duty,
shall not drive a motorcycle or moped
between moving or stationary vehicles occupying adjacent traffic lanes.

elements.justification: 'police officer' (DEF-NRS-484A-180: 'every officer authorized to direct or regulate traffic or to make arrests for violations of traffic laws') is a person's role; the officer's vehicle is of the class ru.emergency_vehicle 'vehicle of a class the jurisdiction designates as emergency; kind in {police, fire, ambulance, other}', read with kind police, whose exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: a responding emergency vehicle' is respected: the class alone is not read as the officer's duty. 'in the performance of his or her duty' is read through the conduct that shows it, the police vehicle displaying its warning lamps: sig.warning_lamp 'a warning lamp lit', mode flashing or rotating; its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: an audible warning' does not apply, no sound is read. Same atoms as the index mapping of '(d) In the performance of official duties;' (NRS_484B_270_3_o2).

'motorcycle' and 'moped' are the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-486-041::motorcycle and DEF-NRS-486-038::moped, claimed as aggregates. 'A person ... shall not drive' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency).

'vehicles' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'moving or stationary' admits either motion state, so no motion is read. 'occupying adjacent traffic lanes': two vehicles v1, v2 occupy (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane') lanes L1, L2 (st.lane, 'a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles') that are adjacent: either neighbours per st.lane_adjacency ('left / right neighbouring lane of the same direction'), or both overlapped by the subject's footprint, which shows they touch whatever their directions. 'between': in the subject's frame v1 lies to its left and v2 to its right (rel.bearing, 'direction of b from a in a's frame (for on the right of ...)', by the sign of its lateral component) and the subject is side by side with each (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero; 'a projection, so neither a contact nor a distance', read only as side-by-side position). The exclusion of st.lane_adjacency ('the marking between two lanes') does not apply. 'traffic lanes' are lanes; the traffic aggregate is not read by the word.

applicability: The subject is of DEF-NRS-486-041::motorcycle or DEF-NRS-486-038::moped, and is not a police vehicle (ru.emergency_vehicle with kind police) displaying a warning lamp (sig.warning_lamp) in mode flashing or rotating, which is read as an officer in the performance of duty (exception s2).
obligation: At every observation there are no two road users v1, v2, each other than the subject and of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, and no two distinct lanes L1, L2 such that v1 occupies L1, v2 occupies L2, L1 and L2 are adjacent (L2 is L1's neighbour per st.lane_adjacency, or the subject occupies both L1 and L2), v1 lies to the subject's left and v2 to its right by rel.bearing, and rel.longitudinal_overlap of the subject with v1 and with v2 is each at or above zero.

narrowings.why: A police officer in the performance of duty is read through conduct: a police vehicle displaying its warning lamps flashing or rotating. An officer on duty riding without lamps is not recognised and is held to the duty.
'A person ... shall not drive' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion; a motorcycle halted between vehicles in traffic is still driven.

Lanes of opposite directions count as adjacent only where the subject's footprint overlaps both; a subject wholly within one lane between a vehicle in that lane and one in an opposing lane is not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A motorcycle straddles the line between same-direction lanes L1 and L2; a car in L1 lies to its left and a car in L2 to its right, each with longitudinal overlap 1 m with the motorcycle.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The motorcycle occupies L1 10 m behind a car in L1; a car in L2 lies to its right with overlap 1 m; nothing lies to its left.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject is a passenger car between two cars in adjacent lanes.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but rel.bearing is not observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A police motorcycle (ru.emergency_vehicle kind police) with blue sig.warning_lamp flashing rides between the two cars as in forbid.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: A police motorcycle with no warning lamp lit rides between the two cars as in forbid.

scenarios.name: branch_2

segmentation.text: Except as provided in subsection 3,
a person shall not drive a motorcycle, moped or trimobile
abreast of or overtake or pass another vehicle within the same traffic lane.
Motorcycles and mopeds may,
with the consent of the drivers,
be operated no more than two abreast in a single traffic lane.

elements.justification: 'motorcycle', 'moped' and 'trimobile' are the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-486-041::motorcycle, DEF-NRS-486-038::moped and DEF-NRS-486-057::trimobile ('every motor vehicle equipped with handlebars and a saddle seat and designed to travel with three wheels'), each claimed as an aggregate. 'a person shall not drive' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency).

'another vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle. 'within the same traffic lane': the subject and the other both occupy one st.lane ('a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles'; rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane'). 'abreast of': rel.longitudinal_overlap 'the bodies overlap along the subject's heading (side by side)' at or above zero; it is 'a projection, so neither a contact nor a distance', read only as side-by-side position. 'overtake or pass ... within the same traffic lane' is read through the same configuration: a pass made within one lane brings the two side by side within that lane, and the duty forbids the place of the pass, so it is judged at every observation the pass is made abreast in the lane; the act concept drv.interaction.overtake_pass, recognised only once the other is behind, would judge the pass after it may have left the lane. 'traffic lane' is a lane; the traffic aggregate is not read by the word.

'Motorcycles and mopeds' are the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-486-041::motorcycle and DEF-NRS-486-038::moped: the exception holds only where both the subject and the other vehicle are of one of them (a trimobile is not named).

The consent of both drivers is not observable; it shows in their conduct of riding together as a pair: rel.same_direction 'headings aligned: the cosine of the angle between the headings is above its tolerance', with tolerance p.side_by_side_same_direction_cos, while abreast within the lane. A pair met head-on in the lane shows no consent.

'no more than two abreast in a single traffic lane': no third road user occupies the same st.lane (rel.occupies) side by side with the subject (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero, 'the bodies overlap along the subject's heading (side by side)'). The figure two is a literal.

residues.why: Points to subsection 3, whose words are this line's second sentence and are carried by s4-s6; the duty is the same whether the pointer is read or not.

applicability: The subject is of DEF-NRS-486-041::motorcycle, DEF-NRS-486-038::moped or DEF-NRS-486-057::trimobile.
obligation: At every observation, for every road user v other than the subject of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle and every lane L that both the subject and v occupy with rel.longitudinal_overlap of subject and v at or above zero, the pair is excused (s4-s6), else the duty is violated. The pair is excused where the subject and v are each of DEF-NRS-486-041::motorcycle or DEF-NRS-486-038::moped, rel.same_direction of subject and v holds with tolerance p.side_by_side_same_direction_cos (consent read), and no third road user w (other than the subject and v) of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle occupies L with rel.longitudinal_overlap of subject and w at or above zero (no more than two abreast).

narrowings.why: The drivers' consent is read through their conduct of riding side by side in the same direction within the lane; an unconsented same-direction pair cannot be told from a consented one and is excused.
'a person shall not drive' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
Overtaking or passing within the same lane is judged at the observations at which the subject is side by side with the other within that lane, not at the recognition of a completed pass.

param_proposals.name: p.side_by_side_same_direction_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest heading difference (about 25 degrees) at which two road users standing or moving side by side count as travelling the same way: the heading spread of vehicles queued in adjacent lanes
param_proposals.source: heading noise of tracked road users in queued traffic
